title: Pseudo-classes and Pseudo-elements
description: Learn how to style elements based on their state or position using pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements.

quiz.question: What is a pseudo-class in CSS?
options: A keyword added to selectors that specifies a special state of the element
An element inserted in the DOM
A type of variable in CSS
quiz.correctAnswer: A keyword added to selectors that specifies a special state of the element
quiz.explanation: Pseudo-classes allow styling elements based on their state like :hover or :focus.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-class applies styles when the user hovers over an element?
quiz.explanation: The :hover pseudo-class applies when a mouse pointer is over an element.

quiz.question: What is a pseudo-element in CSS?
options: A keyword that allows styling a specific part of an element
A type of CSS selector for IDs
quiz.correctAnswer: A keyword that allows styling a specific part of an element
quiz.explanation: Pseudo-elements target parts of an element, such as ::before or ::after.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-element inserts content before the content of an element?
quiz.explanation: ::before inserts generated content before an element's content.

quiz.question: How do you write the syntax for a pseudo-element?
options: Double colon (::) followed by the name
Single colon (:) followed by the name
quiz.correctAnswer: Double colon (::) followed by the name
quiz.explanation: CSS3 uses double colon syntax for pseudo-elements to distinguish from pseudo-classes.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-class targets the first child element of its parent?
quiz.explanation: :first-child and :nth-child(1) both target the first child; :last-child targets the last child.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-class is used to style visited links?
quiz.explanation: :visited applies styles to links that the user has already clicked.

quiz.question: Can pseudo-elements be used to add decorative content without modifying HTML?
quiz.explanation: Pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after allow adding content via CSS.

quiz.question: What pseudo-class can be used to style form elements that are currently focused?
quiz.explanation: :focus applies styles when an element is focused by keyboard or mouse.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-element styles the first letter of a text block?
quiz.explanation: ::first-letter targets the first letter of the text content inside an element.
